program: Perinatal parenting education, postpartum prevention and family counseling
priceScope: Full annual recipient cost against a conditional, partial ROSE-compatible prevention channel; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift expected value.

what: Thriving Families provides MotherWise, La Luz postpartum groups and WiseWellness family counseling in Colorado.
The reference tests postpartum-depression prevention in a hypothetical eligible subgroup, not measured effects across every enrolled family.
Both health and signed net caregiver resources are assessed; the conditional estimate is about $57.9M per better life.
strengths: The La Luz curriculum has a relevant original randomized prevention study against usual care.
Current programs provide childcare and transport, which may reduce participation burdens.
Original three-year full annual expenses and the separate legal recipient were verified.
reservations: Historical enrolled participants are not current unique completed treatments or measured Denver households.
The prenatal ROSE trial does not directly establish local postpartum-program utility, dose or earnings.
Full recipient expenses cover broader work than the modeled prevention subset; other effects remain unknown.

sections.what: The independent legal recipient operates MotherWise, La Luz, WiseWellness and parenting programs. It separated from the University of Denver in 2019. The current official holiday page links the verified recipient ColoradoGives intake; no transaction was made.
sections.monitoring: Request unique annual households by program and ten-county CBSA19740 residence, prenatal versus postpartum eligibility, completed La Luz dose, depression episodes and usual-care referrals. Deduplicate participants, meetings and counseling appointments before tracking work or childcare outcomes.
sections.qualitative: The original ROSE randomized trial enrolled 205 at-risk pregnant adults on public assistance. At six months, depression incidence was 16% versus 31% under usual care. That 15-point difference informs a transferred prevention hypothesis, not an empirical recipient coefficient or measured QALY. Current La Luz is a four-week/six-hour postpartum group. The local eligible share, completion, utility loss and alternative access remain judgments. Marketing claims about preterm birth are not imported without the original study.
sections.cost: FY2024 full annual expenses are $1,929,744, including $30,675 netted direct event costs. The reference pairs these costs with historical FY2023 enrollment of 567 participants, not current unique households. A 0.9 household deduplication factor, 0.25 eligible share, 0.7 completion, 0.5 additionality, 0.15 transferred risk difference, 0.2 utility decrement and half-year episode duration are explicit hypotheses. Denver share 0.9 is judged. Recognized program-cost sensitivity excludes overhead and is not a priced marginal gift.
sections.funding: Usual prenatal/postpartum care, public or insured mental-health services and other charities are alternatives. Net $500 caregiver work resources are after taxes, benefit withdrawal and work expenses, not gross wages; only a judged fraction improves. Full $30 time/access costs and stress remain for all exposed households even when benefits fail. Provided transport/childcare do not prove zero burden. Distinct public payer and provider losses are tested separately, without counting capital grants as household income. A $1M state grant financed the May2024 building, not measured clinical benefits or new donor capacity.

model.costScope: Whole FY2024 legal-recipient annual cost, partial prevention benefit hypothesis; recognized program-only cost scenario is not fully allocated or marginal.
model.geographicAttribution: Ten-county CBSA19740, boundary OMB-23-01-2023-07-21. Beneficiary local share 0.9 is judgment, not headquarters attribution; broader Colorado clients excluded proportionally once.
model.formula: Clinical years = N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted T × g minus full exposed harm. Combined years add signed joint household net consumption welfare using 0.5 × log(1 + net resources / baseline), localized once; price = 10C / positive combined years.
model.counterfactual: Usual prenatal/postpartum care, covered therapy, other parenting groups and household support without this recipient. Trial controls received usual care; recipient additionality and local transfer remain uncertain.
model.attribution: Provider additionality 0.5 is separate from eligible program coverage, completed dose and transferred trial risk difference. No current local causal outcomes observed.
model.uncertainty: Conditional numerical partial-channel reference, not calibrated whole-portfolio expected value. Current completed unique cohort, matching FY2024 outputs, local trial transportability, utility, net resources and marginal capacity unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2023 original filing reports 567 enrolled participants; 572 intakes, 644 family support meetings and 1,720 counseling appointments are overlapping service counts, not additional unique households. Current more-than-700 family growth claim has unspecified vintage. Preterm, other counseling and parenting effects omitted as unknown rather than zero.
